verses.pali: Aṅguttara Nikāya 6.56
verses.english: Numbered Discourses 6.56

verses.pali: 6. Mahāvagga
verses.english: 6. The Great Chapter

verses.pali: Phaggunasutta
verses.english: With Phagguna

verses.pali: Tena kho pana samayena āyasmā phagguno ābādhiko hoti dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: Now at that time Venerable Phagguna was sick, suffering, gravely ill.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “āyasmā, bhante, phagguno ābādhiko dukkhito bāḷhagilāno.
verses.english: “Sir, Venerable Phagguna is sick.

verses.pali: Sādhu, bhante, bhagavā yenāyasmā phagguno tenupasaṅkamatu anukampaṁ upādāyā”ti.
verses.english: Sir, please go to Venerable Phagguna out of sympathy.”

verses.pali: Adhivāsesi bhagavā tuṇhībhāvena.
verses.english: The Buddha consented with silence.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā sāyanhasamayaṁ paṭisallānā vuṭṭhito yenāyasmā phagguno tenupasaṅkami.
verses.english: Then in the late afternoon, the Buddha came out of retreat and went to Venerable Phagguna.

verses.pali: Addasā kho āyasmā phagguno bhagavantaṁ dūratova āgacchantaṁ.
verses.english: Venerable Phagguna saw the Buddha coming off in the distance

verses.pali: Disvāna mañcake samadhosi.
verses.english: and stirred in his cot.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said to him,

verses.pali: “alaṁ, phagguna, mā tvaṁ mañcake samadhosi.
verses.english: “It’s all right, Phagguna, don’t get up.

verses.pali: Santimāni āsanāni parehi paññattāni, tatthāhaṁ nisīdissāmī”ti.
verses.english: There are some seats spread out by others, I will sit there.”

verses.pali: Nisīdi bhagavā paññatte āsane.
verses.english: He sat on the seat spread out

verses.pali: Nisajja kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: and said to Venerable Phagguna:

verses.pali: “Kacci te, phagguna, khamanīyaṁ kacci yāpanīyaṁ? Kacci te dukkhā vedanā paṭikkamanti, no abhikkamanti; paṭikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no abhikkamo”ti?
verses.english: “I hope you’re keeping well, Phagguna; I hope you’re all right. And I hope the pain is fading, not growing, that its fading is evident, not its growing.”

verses.pali: “Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
verses.english: “Sir, I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. The pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso tiṇhena sikharena muddhani abhimattheyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā vātā muddhani ūhananti.
verses.english: The winds piercing my head are so severe, it feels like a strong man drilling into my head with a sharp point.

verses.pali: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
verses.english: I’m not keeping well.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, balavā puriso daḷhena varattakkhaṇḍena sīsaveṭhanaṁ dadeyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā sīse sīsavedanā.
verses.english: The pain in my head is so severe, it feels like a strong man tightening a strong leather strap around my head.

verses.pali: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
verses.english: I’m not keeping well.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, dakkho goghātako vā goghātakantevāsī vā tiṇhena govikantanena kucchiṁ parikanteyya; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimattā vātā kucchiṁ parikantanti.
verses.english: The winds slicing my belly are so severe, like a deft butcher or their apprentice were slicing open a cows’s belly with a sharp meat cleaver.

verses.pali: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo.
verses.english: I’m not keeping well.

verses.pali: Seyyathāpi, bhante, dve balavanto purisā dubbalataraṁ purisaṁ nānābāhāsu gahetvā aṅgārakāsuyā santāpeyyuṁ samparitāpeyyuṁ; evamevaṁ kho me, bhante, adhimatto kāyasmiṁ ḍāho.
verses.english: The burning in my body is so severe, it feels like two strong men grabbing a weaker man by the arms to burn and scorch him on a pit of glowing coals.

verses.pali: Na me, bhante, khamanīyaṁ na yāpanīyaṁ. Bāḷhā me dukkhā vedanā abhikkamanti, no paṭikkamanti; abhikkamosānaṁ paññāyati, no paṭikkamo”ti.
verses.english: I’m not keeping well, I’m not getting by. The pain is terrible and growing, not fading; its growing is evident, not its fading.”

verses.pali: Atha kho bhagavā āyasmantaṁ phaggunaṁ dhammiyā kathāya sandassetvā samādapetvā samuttejetvā sampahaṁsetvā uṭṭhāyāsanā pakkāmi.
verses.english: Then the Buddha educated, encouraged, fired up, and inspired Venerable Phagguna with a Dhamma talk, after which he got up from his seat and left.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā phagguno acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi.
verses.english: Not long after the Buddha left, Venerable Phagguna passed away.

verses.pali: Tamhi cassa samaye maraṇakāle indriyāni vippasīdiṁsu.
verses.english: At the time of his death, his faculties were bright and clear.

verses.pali: Atha kho āyasmā ānando yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho āyasmā ānando bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Venerable Ānanda went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him,

verses.pali: “āyasmā, bhante, phagguno acirapakkantassa bhagavato kālamakāsi.
verses.english: “Sir, soon after the Buddha left, Venerable Phagguna died.

verses.pali: Tamhi cassa samaye maraṇakāle indriyāni vippasīdiṁsū”ti.
verses.english: At the time of his death, his faculties were bright and clear.”

verses.pali: “Kiṁ hānanda, phaggunassa bhikkhuno indriyāni na vippasīdissanti.
verses.english: “And why shouldn’t his faculties be bright and clear?

verses.pali: Phaggunassa, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ ahosi.
verses.english: The mendicant Phagguna’s mind was not freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ.
verses.english: But when he heard that teaching his mind was freed from them.

verses.pali: Chayime, ānanda, ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
verses.english: Ānanda, there are these six benefits to hearing the teaching at the right time and examining the meaning at the right time.

verses.pali: Katame cha?
verses.english: What six?

verses.pali: Idhānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Firstly, take the case of a mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: At the time of death they get to see the Realized One.

verses.pali: Tassa tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
verses.english: The Realized One proclaims a teaching to them that is good in the beginning, good in the middle, and good in the end, meaningful and well-phrased. And he reveals a spiritual practice that’s entirely full and pure.

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, paṭhamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
verses.english: This is the first benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, api ca kho tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya.
verses.english: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, but they get to see a Realized One’s disciple.

verses.pali: Tassa tathāgatasāvako dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ pariyosānakalyāṇaṁ sātthaṁ sabyañjanaṁ, kevalaparipuṇṇaṁ parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
verses.english: The Realized One’s disciple teaches them Dhamma …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, dutiyo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
verses.english: This is the second benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is not freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, napi tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya;
verses.english: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, or to see a Realized One’s disciple.

verses.pali: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
verses.english: But they think about and consider the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Tassa yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakkayato anuvicārayato manasānupekkhato pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: As they do so their mind is freed from the five lower fetters.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, tatiyo ānisaṁso kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
verses.english: This is the third benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Idhānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Next, take the case of a mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya.
verses.english: At the time of death they get to see the Realized One.

verses.pali: Tassa tathāgato dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ majjhekalyāṇaṁ …pe… brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
verses.english: The Realized One teaches them Dhamma …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, catuttho ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
verses.english: This is the fourth benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, api ca kho tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya.
verses.english: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, but they get to see a Realized One’s disciple.

verses.pali: Tassa tathāgatasāvako dhammaṁ deseti ādikalyāṇaṁ …pe… parisuddhaṁ brahmacariyaṁ pakāseti.
verses.english: The Realized One’s disciple teaches them Dhamma …

verses.pali: Tassa taṁ dhammadesanaṁ sutvā anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: When they hear that teaching their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, pañcamo ānisaṁso kālena dhammassavane.
verses.english: This is the fifth benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Puna caparaṁ, ānanda, bhikkhuno pañcahi orambhāgiyehi saṁyojanehi cittaṁ vimuttaṁ hoti, anuttare ca kho upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ avimuttaṁ hoti.
verses.english: Next, take the case of another mendicant whose mind is freed from the five lower fetters, but not with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: So tamhi samaye maraṇakāle na heva kho labhati tathāgataṁ dassanāya, napi tathāgatasāvakaṁ labhati dassanāya;
verses.english: At the time of death they don’t get to see the Realized One, or to see a Realized One’s disciple.

verses.pali: api ca kho yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakketi anuvicāreti manasānupekkhati.
verses.english: But they think about and consider the teaching in their heart, examining it with the mind as they learned and memorized it.

verses.pali: Tassa yathāsutaṁ yathāpariyattaṁ dhammaṁ cetasā anuvitakkayato anuvicārayato manasānupekkhato anuttare upadhisaṅkhaye cittaṁ vimuccati.
verses.english: As they do so their mind is freed with the supreme ending of attachments.

verses.pali: Ayaṁ, ānanda, chaṭṭho ānisaṁso kālena atthupaparikkhāya.
verses.english: This is the sixth benefit of listening to the teaching.

verses.pali: Ime kho, ānanda, cha ānisaṁsā kālena dhammassavane kālena atthupaparikkhāyā”ti.
verses.english: These are the six benefits to hearing the teaching at the right time and examining the meaning at the right time.”

verses.pali: Dutiyaṁ.
